title: Tranexamic acid vs. embolization of the meningeal artery as an adjunctive therapeutic regime to reduce the recurrence rate after surgical relief of chronic subdural hematomas - a randomized controlled trial.
summary:
Chronic subdural haematoma (cSDH) is a persistent bloody fluid build-up underneath the meninges. If it displaces the brain and causes neurological deficits, it is relieved surgically. After surgery, however, recurrent bleeding or increasing fluid retention is common. The aim of this study is to compare two supportive therapy measures that are used after surgery with regard to their effectiveness in preventing the recurrence of bleeding. The therapeutic procedures to be investigated are, on the one hand, a drug therapy with a drug that influences blood clotting and, on the other hand, a procedure in which a fine tube is inserted via a vessel in the groin or forearm in order to introduce tiny particles into the vessels of the head that supply the meninges with blood, under the control of an X-ray machine and the administration of contrast medium, in order to seal them. 
Patients can take part in this study if they are of legal age and have undergone surgery for a chronic subdural hematoma immediately before participating in the study by means of a so-called borehole trepanation, i.e. the surgical creation of a single hole in the skull bone. Patients are randomly assigned to the test group with drug therapy following the operation or the control group with occlusion of blood vessels in the head. To record the test results, control examinations are carried out after 1 week and at monthly intervals up to a total of 3 months after inclusion in the study. Neurological tests and radiological examinations are carried out during the check-ups.

interventions.name: Postoperative adjuvant drug therapy with tranexamic acid
Postoperative adjuvant embolization of the middle meningeal artery on the affected side using digital subtraction angiography

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. patients who underwent surgery for unilateral cSDH for the first time no more than 24 hours before inclusion in the study.
2. written consent to participate in the study by the patient or a legal representative
Exclusion criteria:
1. Conservatively treated cSDH
2. Bilateral cSDH
3. Age < 18 years 
4. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
5. radiological evidence of an acute subdural hematoma, subarachnoid hemorrhage, epidural or intracerebral hematoma
6. structural causes of subdural hemorrhages, e.g. arachnoid cysts, cortical vascular malformations 
7. Lack of patient information in the absence of legal guardianship
8. inability to perform angiography/embolization within 72 hours of the operation if there are contraindications to taking tranexamic acid (inability to cross over)
9. Embolization not technically feasible
10. Condition after borehole trepanation, craniotomies and craniectomies for other reasons in the past
